sections.h2: Where in Raleigh do you take a deed for Wake County?
sections.html:
Go to the Wake County Justice Center, 300 S. Salisbury St., Suite 1700, Raleigh, NC 27601. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.; the office answers at 919-856-5460 or rodinfo@wake.gov.

The county calls the register a custodian of a very large body of public records. Land documents share the counter with marriage licenses, birth and death certificate copies, business name filings, nuptial agreements and restrictive covenants.

A seller with a Raleigh-area house rarely goes in person. Your closing firm files the deed, which is the step that publishes the sale.

sections.h2: How much does Wake County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
On the register's schedule, an ordinary deed starts at $26 and a deed of trust at $64, with $4 for each page past the included count.

Wake County register fee schedule, items a home sale may touch
ItemWake County price
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 covers 35 pages; $4 per page after
Amendment to a deed of trust$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per page after
Other instruments, including assumed names$26 covers 15 pages; $4 per page after
Non-standard layout$25 on top of the recording fee
Each additional instrument bundled in a document$10 each
Satisfaction of a security instrumentFree
Plat or condominium map$21 a page
Certified copy$5 for page one; $2 for each later page
Deed excise tax from August 1, 1991$2 per thousand

Large filings pay $2 for each party name beyond twenty, and an assignment's first added deed of trust reference is free.

sections.h2: What counts as a standard deed in Wake County?
sections.html:
Missing any single item on the register's standard-document list triggers the $25 surcharge, and the list covers layout only.

  • Paper sized 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches at the top of the first page, with half-inch margins everywhere else.
  • Black print on white paper in at least 9 point.
  • One side only, with the instrument type centered on page one.

Pen is acceptable for filling blanks and making corrections. Documents from a title firm pass as a matter of course. A form downloaded and printed double-sided, or a scan that crowds the edge, is the sort of file that draws the extra $25.

sections.h2: How is the Wake County deed transfer tax stated?
sections.html:
The fee page lists $2 per thousand for deeds since August 1, 1991, and the help page for changing names on a deed mentions the same excise tax on a purchase price.

State law words it as a dollar per $500 and makes the transferor pay first, so the seller sees it at settlement. Ask the closing office for the number on your deed.

The fee page also lists $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1969, which matter when reading an old transfer.

sections.h2: What can you search through the Wake County register's index?
sections.html:
The county says its public records start in 1785, and the Consolidated Real Property Index lets a seller or a buyer's lawyer follow title from a desk.

Start with your own deed and compare its legal description and owner names against the contract. Next, look for the deed of trust you are paying off, and after closing look for its satisfaction, which the fee page lists at no charge.

A fraud alert service emails you when a monitored name appears on a recorded document, handy for heirs, landlords and owners of empty houses.

sections.h2: What should be ready before a Wake County deed goes in?
sections.html:
The package is a signed, acknowledged deed that meets the layout rules, plus payment. Firms handle it for most sellers, but someone recording a family transfer may do it alone.

  • Names written as on the previous deed, since the index is searched by name.
  • Recording fee, plus excise tax if the transfer is a sale.
  • Any added instrument, which carries its own $10 charge when bundled.

The register suggests an attorney for any drafting question. A wrong legal description or missing signature goes back to whoever prepared the deed, and adding or removing an owner means recording a new deed.

sections.h2: How does the register connect to Wake County tax records?
sections.html:
Two county departments touch the house. The register records the ownership paper, while Tax Administration appraises and bills. Settle the tax bill through closing.

The tax help line is 919-856-5400. Wake also bills towns and special districts, so one bill can carry several charges. The county's bill page reports 53.71 cents after a 2-cent increase adopted for Fiscal Year 2027.

Values reset on January 1, 2027, the effective date of the county's next revaluation, which sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods.

sections.h2: What should a Wake County seller line up with the register and the tax office?
sections.html:
None of this needs a trip downtown if a closing firm is involved.

  • Your recorded deed, pulled from the online index.
  • The payoff letter for any deed of trust, followed by a recorded release at no charge.
  • A tax figure from Tax Administration, which matters most for owners who pay by escrow and never see a bill.
  • A deed laid out to the standard list.

Heirs unsure what is recorded can search the index, then phone 919-856-5460. The register suggests an attorney for questions about the deed itself.

sections.h2: Which Wake County register services help heirs selling an inherited house?
sections.html:
The register sells certified death certificates, which heirs often need for estate paperwork. The fee page lists $10 per certified copy, with a $10 amendment charge, and for out-of-county death certificates a $14 search fee, a $10 certified copy and $15 for each additional copy. Ordering online adds a county charge of $10 per copy plus a vendor convenience fee that varies.

The same fee page lists copies of recorded documents. A certified copy of a document is $5 for page one and $2 for each page after, and the county does not charge for its trailer page. A certified copy of a map is $5.

  • Get a certified deed copy to show how the decedent held title.
  • Check the index for any open deed of trust before listing the house.
  • Ask an attorney whether probate steps must come before a deed is recorded.

The register does not decide who may sign a deed for an estate. That question belongs to the probate side and to your attorney.

sections.h2: Does Wake County record anything besides deeds that affects a house?
sections.html:
Yes. The fee page lists plats and condominium maps at $21 per page, right-of-way plans and highway maps at $21 for the first page and $5 for each page after, and UCC filings at $38 each for the UCC-1 and UCC-3, rising to $45 above two pages. The county's example prices a 13-page UCC filing at $51.

For a seller, the useful items are the maps and restrictive covenants, since both can describe limits on the parcel. The register's description says restrictive covenants and survey maps are recorded here, and its index reaches back to 1785. Ask your title or closing firm to pull any plat and covenant that applies to your subdivision.

Business owners operating from home may also file an assumed name here, which the fee page places at the $26 instrument rate.

sections.h2: Does the Wake County register take e-recording?
sections.html:
Ask the office or your closing firm how a deed will be sent and what cutoff applies. Paper goes to the Justice Center on weekdays.

For any question tied to a particular filing, call 919-856-5460 before you go.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter after a Wake County sale?
sections.html:
Until a conveyance is registered in the county where the land lies, it carries no weight against lien creditors or purchasers for value. For a Raleigh-area house, that makes the filing the buyer's protection.

File the stamped copy with your closing papers and confirm the old lender's release is recorded.

faqs.q: Is the Wake County deed office open on Saturdays?
faqs.a: No. The Justice Center office keeps weekday hours only. Call 919-856-5460 about holidays.

faqs.q: How is Wake County's deed excise tax stated?
faqs.a: The county lists it as $2 per thousand on deeds since August 1, 1991; the transferor pays.

faqs.q: Does Wake County charge to record a payoff release?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are listed as free.

faqs.q: How do I change the names on a Wake County deed?
faqs.a: With a new deed. The register suggests an attorney unless you are used to preparing legal papers.
